description: Add server-side auth guard to the admin panel so all /admin/* sub-pages (not just the dashboard) redirect unauthenticated users to /admin/login. Implemented via Next.js middleware.ts at the repo root, which is the correct pattern for route-level auth in Next.js App Router. The admin layout is converted to a server component (sidebar only, no auth logic).
steps: Step 1 — Create middleware.ts at repo root (e:\work\raghul-snacks\raghul-snacks\middleware.ts). The middleware matches all /admin/* routes and excludes /admin/login. For matched routes, it reads the admin session cookie using the same cookie name and validation logic as lib/admin-auth.ts. If the cookie is invalid/absent, it redirects to /admin/login. Important: middleware.ts runs in the Next.js Edge Runtime. The lib/admin-auth.ts uses Node.js crypto (createHmac, timingSafeEqual) which is NOT available in the Edge Runtime. Therefore, re-implement the HMAC validation inline in middleware.ts using the Web Crypto API (SubtleCrypto). The cookie name is 'raghul_admin_session' (hardcoded — same as adminCookieName() returns). The validation logic: split the cookie value on '.', check payload === 'admin', compute HMAC-SHA256 of 'admin' using ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET, compare in constant time. Use: const encoder = new TextEncoder(); const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', encoder.encode(secret), { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' }, false, ['verify']); const valid = await crypto.subtle.verify('HMAC', key, hexToBytes(signature), encoder.encode(payload)); where hexToBytes converts hex string to Uint8Array. If validation passes, call next(); otherwise redirect to /admin/login.

Step 2 — Convert app/admin/layout.tsx from client to server component. Remove the 'use client' directive. Remove the usePathname import and usage. The layout simply renders the sidebar and main content for all routes — auth is now handled by middleware. The resulting layout: import AdminSidebar, import styles, export default function AdminLayout({ children }) { return (
{children}
); }. Note: AdminSidebar is a client component ('use client') — this is fine, server components can render client component children. The login page (/admin/login) will be handled by the middleware (matcher excludes it), so the layout correctly wraps only authenticated pages.

Step 3 — Verify the matcher in middleware.ts correctly excludes /admin/login. The matcher config should be: export const config = { matcher: ['/admin/:path*'] }. Inside the middleware handler, add an early return for the login page: if (request.nextUrl.pathname === '/admin/login') return NextResponse.next(). This ensures the login page is never redirected.
acceptance_criteria: middleware.ts uses Web Crypto API (not Node.js crypto) for HMAC validation — compatible with Edge Runtime
Navigating to /admin/orders without an admin session cookie redirects to /admin/login
app/admin/layout.tsx has no 'use client' directive and no usePathname usage
findings: middleware.ts created at repo root using Web Crypto API (SubtleCrypto) for HMAC-SHA256 validation — fully Edge Runtime compatible. hexToBytes returns Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> (not ArrayBufferLike) to satisfy TypeScript strict type checking. app/admin/layout.tsx converted to server component with no 'use client' directive and no usePathname usage. Build exits 0. Lint on changed files exits 0. Pre-existing lint errors in other files (wishlist-provider.tsx, etc.) are unrelated to this feature. Next.js 16 emits a deprecation warning that 'middleware' convention is renamed to 'proxy' — this is a warning only, not an error, and the file still works correctly.
